title: Severed Robot Hand Looks Like a Futuristic Thing From The Addams Family
summary:
Halloween is just around the corner, and engineers have built a spooky robot: a detached hand inspired by Thing from The Addams Family. Like its gothic sitcom predecessor, this fully articulated hand can balance on its own fingertips and creep around. It can tap keyboard keys, push small objects and even play a simple computer game while balancing on its remaining fingers. If it falls, it can recover and lift itself up from a flat position.

Walking robot hands are not new, but earlier efforts mostly required changing the hand's structure, such as making every finger the same length so it could balance. Human hands have uneven fingers and an opposable thumb, which helps us use many tools but is not well suited for upright walking. A team from the Soft Robotics Lab at ETH Zurich in Switzerland set out to solve that problem, according to a recent preprint, a paper that has not yet been peer-reviewed.

The team began with an off-the-shelf mechanical hand designed for humanoid robots, with five fingers and 20 actuated joints. They mounted a battery, motion sensors and a tiny computer on the back, and the whole robot weighs 1.8 pounds. They taught it to balance in a simulation using reinforcement learning, which rewarded the software every time the hand balanced correctly. Each finger was assigned its own target position, so where and when each finger moved depended on the task.

In real-world tests, the hand crossed 14 different indoor and outdoor environments, including carpet, gravel, grass and metal, with a springy, spider-like gait. It balanced on several fingers while using the others to push a small cube. In testing, it hit the correct keys 29 out of 32 times when typing, and it played the puzzle game Sokoban by pressing arrow keys in sequence.

The team notes that these skills could serve a more important purpose than a creepy Halloween decoration. In the future, humanoid robots working in cramped areas could detach a hand and send it to retrieve an item. The researchers write: "Giving robotic hands their own mobility could make future robots more versatile in the spaces and interfaces built for people." Improvements in finger control and balance might also help robot hands handle objects designed for human hands.
why_it_matters: The work shows how engineers solve odd design problems, and it could lead to robot hands that are better at using objects made for human hands.

keywords.explanation: Having joints that let parts move separately.
A thumb that can touch the other fingers, which helps people grip objects.

questions.question: Why did earlier walking robot hands need design changes?
options: They needed several extra thumbs to hold a heavy battery pack
They needed to be much larger than a normal human hand
They needed to be powered by large solar panels outside
They needed every finger to be the same length to balance
questions.correct_answer: They needed every finger to be the same length to balance

questions.question: What kind of hand did the ETH Zurich team start with?
options: An off-the-shelf mechanical hand for humanoid robots
A glove with small built-in lights for the dark
A hand carved by hand from a block of wood
A hand taken from a mannequin in a clothing store
questions.correct_answer: An off-the-shelf mechanical hand for humanoid robots

questions.question: How was each finger controlled during training?
options: A person moved the fingers by remote control
Each finger was assigned its own target position
Each finger stayed completely still until the very end
All of the fingers were forced to move together
questions.correct_answer: Each finger was assigned its own target position

questions.question: How many environments did the hand cross in real-world tests?
options: 2 indoor rooms
20 beaches
7 school hallways
14 indoor and outdoor environments

questions.question: Which game did the hand play by pressing arrow keys?
options: Pac-Man
Minecraft
Sokoban
Chess

questions.question: What does the preprint note mean for this research?
options: It was published in a famous textbook
It has been proven by thousands of tests
It has not yet been peer-reviewed
It was rejected by every scientist
questions.correct_answer: It has not yet been peer-reviewed

background_read: Peer review is when other experts check a scientific paper before it is published in a journal.
